name: MarkLab: slides to research results
purpose: Turn prepared pathology observations into measurements of tissue composition, architecture and spatial organization, then compare those measurements across regions, sections or patients.

starting_point.raw_slide_only: MarkLab can inspect slide metadata and extract bounded image regions. Biological analysis needs cells, measurements, vectors or annotations produced upstream.
starting_point.prepared_slide: Calibrated cell coordinates and the observed tissue window unlock point-pattern analysis. Labels, marker values, tissue polygons and embeddings unlock additional questions.
starting_point.full_pipeline: Study design -> slide preparation -> upstream feature extraction -> import/alignment -> per-slide measurements -> patient summaries -> inference or modeling -> research outputs.
starting_point.execution: This is a composable research pipeline. MarkLab has several integrated workflows, but no single command ingests a raw slide and automatically runs every analysis.

input_to_output.get: Image metadata and selected pixel regions.
input_to_output.enables: Prepare regions for external segmentation, measurements or review.

input_to_output.provide: Cell coordinates + physical calibration + observation window
input_to_output.get: Cell density, spacing, clustering/regularity curves, empty-space and structural descriptors.
input_to_output.enables: Study how densely and regularly cells occupy the tissue.

input_to_output.provide: The above + cell types, binary labels, probabilities or marker intensities
input_to_output.get: Composition, phenotype organization, type-to-type mixing, neighborhood diversity, marker smoothness and hotspots.
input_to_output.enables: Study heterogeneity and the spatial context of measured or predicted cell states.

input_to_output.provide: Tissue/compartment/epithelium polygons, with optional nuclear measurements
input_to_output.get: Boundary gradients, compartment contact/fragmentation, invasive-front bands, epithelial architecture and nuclear shape summaries.
input_to_output.enables: Study tumor-stroma relationships, architecture and changes near the invasive front.

input_to_output.provide: Cell or patch embeddings with exact object/coordinate links
input_to_output.get: Morphology-feature similarity across distance, multiscale variation, cross-modal relationships and analogous-region retrieval.
input_to_output.enables: Study tissue morphology beyond predefined cell classes or shape measurements.

input_to_output.provide: Multiple stains, registered capture spots, serial sections or repeated samples
input_to_output.get: Cross-stain relationships, spot architecture coverage, 3-D spatial summaries or between-section/timepoint changes.
input_to_output.enables: Connect observations across modalities, physical sections and time.

input_to_output.provide: Multiple patients with groups, covariates or held-out outcomes
input_to_output.get: Patient-level contrasts, uncertainty, adjusted tests and selected hierarchical or prediction models.
input_to_output.enables: Test whether tissue measurements differ between biological groups or add predictive information.

pipeline.stage: 1. Define the research question and sampling design
work: Choose the biological comparison and primary measurements.
Declare patients, groups, slides, regions, timepoints and repeated samples.
Choose observation windows, spatial scales, null models, covariates and multiplicity families.
Prespecify equivalence margins or patient-held-out splits when relevant.
pipeline.produces: A declared study design; cells and patches are not treated as independent patients.

pipeline.stage: 2. Prepare the slide and observed region
pipeline.performed_by: Upstream imaging/QC tools and researcher; optional MarkLab image reader
work: Acquire the slide and establish physical pixel scale, axes and section identity.
Select the observed tissue or sampled regions and exclude folds, tears, blur and other artifacts upstream.
Supply a tissue/observation mask, preserving holes and disconnected pieces.
Optionally inspect WSI metadata or extract bounded regions with MarkLab.
pipeline.produces: Calibrated image regions and an explicit observation window.
pipeline.boundary: The WSI reader does not automatically segment tissue, detect artifacts or establish biological calibration.

pipeline.stage: 3. Extract cells, labels, measurements and tissue structures
pipeline.performed_by: External models, measurement tools or manual annotation
work: Detect/segment nuclei or cells and export stable IDs and centroids.
Supply cell types, phenotype labels or full class probabilities as needed.
Measure staining channels and nuclear morphology when those are the research inputs.
Optionally generate cell/patch embeddings or annotate epithelium, stroma, vessels, lumens, mucin and architecture classes.
pipeline.produces: Cell tables, vectors and polygons with their source and measurement/prediction status.
pipeline.boundary: CellViT is one optional producer. MarkLab does not require it and does not itself run cell segmentation, architecture classification or image-encoder training.

work: Read the supported cell, vector and polygon profiles; map other exports into those contracts.
Check identities, finite values, physical coordinates, window inclusion, missingness and resource limits.
Keep cells, marks and embeddings aligned by declared identity.
For multiple sections, supply or fit the relevant registration and assess its uncertainty.
For cell/patch/region features, declare footprints, overlap and aggregation links.
pipeline.produces: Validated, coordinate-aligned observations ready for the chosen analyses.
available_paths: Explicit cell-table and bounded AnnData adapters
Selected QuPath, Steinbock, MCMICRO and normalized CellViT adapters
Generic NPY and strict embedding Arrow/Parquet artifacts
Landmark H&E/IHC alignment and separate nonrigid/uncertainty workflows
pipeline.boundary: Import does not infer unknown scale, patient identity, cell type or correspondence. General native project formats may need external conversion.

pipeline.performed_by: MarkLab; select branches that match the question and available inputs
work: Measure composition/density and cell spacing.
Measure label organization, cell-type interactions and neighborhoods.
Map marker gradients, hotspots and annotation-relative profiles.
Measure epithelial architecture, front-distance bands, budding candidates and supplied nuclear shapes.
Optionally compute embedding, graph, topology or 3-D features.
pipeline.produces: Per-cell, per-region or per-slide measurements, spatial curves and maps; selected methods also provide null tests and uncertainty.
pipeline.boundary: Different branches answer different questions. Descriptive outputs do not automatically have p-values, and all branches do not run together by default.

pipeline.stage: 6. Convert slide measurements into patient-level endpoints
pipeline.performed_by: Built-in study workflows or explicit researcher-defined aggregation
work: Link observations from the same patient and distinguish repeated samples from independent patients.
Use a pooling rule appropriate to each measurement.
Retain missing/unavailable results instead of filling them with zeros.
For custom graph, architecture or embedding endpoints, prepare a compatible patient-level table.

implemented_pooling.multiplex_study: Mean of a patient's slide-level Moran/Geary values, followed by equal patient weighting.
implemented_pooling.pathology_composition: Pool cell counts and observed areas across a patient's slides before calculating composition/density.
implemented_pooling.pathology_spatial_study: Area-weighted patient mean curves on a common supported distance axis.

pipeline.produces: A patient-by-measurement table or patient-level curves suitable for the declared study design.
pipeline.boundary: There is no universal averaging rule or automatic conversion of every result document into a cohort input.

pipeline.stage: 7. Test the research hypothesis or fit a model
pipeline.performed_by: MarkLab with a declared design; selected methods use locked Python workers
work: Compare groups or paired observations with patient/cluster-aware tests and multiplicity correction.
Estimate uncertainty, equivalence or noninferiority under prespecified margins.
Account for selected covariates, sites and hierarchical sampling.
Optionally fit spatial/hierarchical models, evaluate held-out predictors or compare simulations with observations.
pipeline.produces: Effect estimates, intervals, adjusted tests, model diagnostics or held-out predictions.
pipeline.boundary: Single-slide spatial evidence and population-level evidence are separate. Prediction and mechanistic/causal modeling require additional data and assumptions.

pipeline.performed_by: MarkLab exports; researcher interprets and validates
work: Export structured results and available supporting tables, curves, reports, figures or GeoJSON layers.
Review QC, unavailable measurements, registration sensitivity and model convergence.
Apply recorded coordinate transforms before overlaying physical-coordinate maps on image pixels.
Use selected durable project/study workflows to resume and reuse unchanged work.
pipeline.produces: Research endpoints and reviewable spatial evidence for downstream statistics, figures and manuscripts.
pipeline.boundary: Available files differ by workflow; not every command generates every report or plot.

composition_and_cellularity.question: What cells are present, and how much of each type is there?
composition_and_cellularity.research_use: Compare immune/tumor abundance or distinguish a change in relative composition from a change in absolute density.
composition_and_cellularity.access: pathology composition; typed-mark Rust analyses; basic count/density summaries in other workflows

cell_spacing_and_clustering.question: Are cells clustered, evenly dispersed or separated by empty space, and at what distances?
cell_spacing_and_clustering.needs: Cell positions and a calibrated observation window; types if testing selected populations.
cell_spacing_and_clustering.research_use: Compare compact versus dispersed arrangements, focal aggregates and organization at multiple physical scales.
cell_spacing_and_clustering.access: classical, nearest-space, project spatial methods, pathology spatial-study

phenotype_heterogeneity.question: Is a phenotype such as MMR loss or marker positivity spatially patchy, directional or organized at a characteristic scale?
phenotype_heterogeneity.needs: Cell positions and a binary or probabilistic phenotype label.
phenotype_heterogeneity.research_use: Quantify mosaic staining and compare organization even when two sections have similar overall positivity.
phenotype_heterogeneity.access: analyze, batch, prepost; typed mark/probability methods

cell_type_relationships.question: Which cell populations occur together, mix or avoid one another?
cell_type_relationships.needs: Coordinates and declared cell classes or probabilities; compartment annotations for boundary-specific questions.
cell_type_relationships.research_use: Describe immune-tumor proximity, stromal separation or relationships among supplied immune subsets.
cell_type_relationships.access: numerics categorical methods, project cross-type methods, multimodal neighborhoods, compartment Rust analyses

local_neighborhoods.question: What cellular environment surrounds each cell?
local_neighborhoods.needs: Cell positions and hard classes or complete class probabilities.
get: Dominant-versus-mixed composition maps at chosen radii
local_neighborhoods.research_use: Compare tumor-rich, immune-rich and mixed local environments, including their scale dependence.
local_neighborhoods.access: pathology maps; soft/categorical neighborhood Rust methods
local_neighborhoods.boundary: These summarize supplied classes; MarkLab does not train a niche-discovery model.

marker_fields_and_gradients.question: How does a marker vary across tissue and with distance from a structure?
marker_fields_and_gradients.needs: Per-cell marker values; annotations for tumor borders, vessels or other reference structures.
get: Marker and density profiles inside/outside annotations
Optional field interpolation or resource-distance models
marker_fields_and_gradients.research_use: Study proliferation gradients, perivascular organization or marker variation across tumor-stroma boundaries.
marker_fields_and_gradients.access: pathology maps, study, scalar variograms, ordinary kriging, distance-to-resource models

hotspots_and_outliers.question: Where are unusually concentrated cells or locally unusual marker values?
hotspots_and_outliers.needs: Coordinates, target labels or marker values, and prespecified scan/neighborhood/null settings.
get: Best qualifying enriched circular region per slide
Search- or location-adjusted tests where supported
hotspots_and_outliers.research_use: Find focal aggregates or heterogeneous staining regions for independent review and follow-up sampling.
hotspots_and_outliers.access: pathology scan, pathology maps, analyze residual territories
hotspots_and_outliers.boundary: A search region is not an inferred lesion boundary; residual territories and hypothesis-tested hotspots have different meanings.

tissue_architecture_and_front.question: How does tumor architecture change from the tumor interior across its advancing edge?
tissue_architecture_and_front.needs: Epithelium and observation polygons, declared architecture regions, optional lumen/mucin/front exclusions and epithelial cell counts.
get: Derived tumor bulk/front and signed distance bands
Component size, fragmentation, lumen containment and contour irregularity
Budding candidates and a front-centered hotspot
tissue_architecture_and_front.research_use: Quantify architecture transitions, epithelial fragmentation and reviewed budding patterns near an invasive front.
tissue_architecture_and_front.boundary: Architecture labels and segmentation come from upstream. Operational budding counts need biological/pathologist validation.

nuclear_morphology.question: How do nuclear shape and orientation vary with phenotype and tissue position?
nuclear_morphology.needs: Upstream nuclear area/perimeter/axes/orientation, epithelial labels and optional front geometry or embeddings.
get: Selected binary-group area contrasts and embedding relationships
nuclear_morphology.research_use: Study nuclear morphology in different epithelial architectures, phenotypes or front-distance bands.
nuclear_morphology.access: pathology architecture; nuclear-area and embedding Rust analyses
nuclear_morphology.boundary: Elongation/alignment describe shape; they do not directly measure mechanical force.

structural_fingerprints.question: Can tissue organization be represented by multiscale quantitative features?
structural_fingerprints.needs: Points, masks or declared graphs with signals; optional feature vectors.
get: Connected components, loops and persistence summaries
Packing orientation, gap heterogeneity and selected density-fluctuation descriptors
structural_fingerprints.research_use: Construct exploratory tissue signatures and compare their sensitivity to sampling, scale or segmentation.
structural_fingerprints.boundary: These are selectable research features, not one automatic or validated diagnostic fingerprint.

morphology_embeddings.question: How does learned morphology vary across space, and what does it add beyond measured markers?
morphology_embeddings.needs: Externally generated cell/patch/region vectors with exact identities, coordinates and model declarations; measured modalities for comparison.
get: Feature similarity and covariance by distance
morphology_embeddings.research_use: Link morphology to protein measurements, explore heterogeneity beyond hand-defined classes, or test whether multiple feature scales add information.
morphology_embeddings.access: Embedding Rust analyses; selected bayes, multimodal and project commands
morphology_embeddings.boundary: MarkLab analyzes supplied vectors; it does not generate them from slide pixels or automatically infer molecular states.

cross_stain_and_spot_context.question: How do observations from different stains or spatial capture spots relate to tissue context?
cross_stain_and_spot_context.needs: Calibrated H&E/IHC cells plus landmarks, or registered spot centers/diameters and architecture polygons.
get: Fractions of each spot covered by tissue, tumor bulk and architecture classes
cross_stain_and_spot_context.research_use: Connect morphology with staining or attach a quantitative histologic context to spatial transcriptomic measurements.
cross_stain_and_spot_context.access: multimodal analyze; pathology architecture; optional nonrigid registration
cross_stain_and_spot_context.boundary: Expression tables join downstream by spot ID; this is not a complete transcriptomics preprocessing or deconvolution pipeline.

patient_group_comparisons.question: Do these tissue measurements differ between patient groups?
patient_group_comparisons.needs: Multiple independent patients, group labels and compatible slide/patient endpoints; relevant covariates/sites/blocks.
get: Paired, covariate, clustered or multisite designs
patient_group_comparisons.research_use: Compare tumor subtypes, molecular groups or treatment groups while respecting patient-level replication.
patient_group_comparisons.access: study; pathology composition/spatial-study; cohort; Bayesian hierarchies
patient_group_comparisons.boundary: A single slide provides specimen-level observations. Population claims need independent patients and the appropriate design.

changes_across_time_and_sections.question: How does organization differ across paired samples, timepoints or serial sections?
changes_across_time_and_sections.needs: Compatible paired results, repeated observations or serial sections with spacing/registration and declared uncertainty.
changes_across_time_and_sections.research_use: Characterize paired tissue changes or reconstruct spatial organization across a section series.
changes_across_time_and_sections.boundary: Different sections do not track the same cells. Timepoint change alone does not establish treatment causation.

predictive_and_mechanistic_research.question: Do tissue features help prediction, or are they consistent with a proposed generating process?
predictive_and_mechanistic_research.needs: For prediction: patient outcomes and held-out designs. For models: process assumptions/priors or simulations. For causal effects: an identified experimental/observational design.
get: Selected held-out prediction/fusion, calibration and OOD analyses
Spatial intensity and interaction models with diagnostics
Interference effects, sensitivity bounds or active-design calculations
predictive_and_mechanistic_research.research_use: Evaluate candidate research biomarkers, compare spatial hypotheses and plan follow-up experiments.
predictive_and_mechanistic_research.access: Selected bayes/multimodal prediction and model commands; simulate, neural, causal
predictive_and_mechanistic_research.boundary: These are additional research workflows. A matching simulation does not identify a mechanism, and a predictive association does not establish clinical utility or causation.

integrated_workflows.chain: Prepared marked cells + window -> QC -> spatial label statistics/nulls -> section result and supporting outputs.
Manifest -> repeated marked analyses; compatible completed analyses -> paired section comparison.
H&E/IHC cells + landmarks -> registration -> cell fusion -> graph -> enrichment, cross-curves and territories.
Declared multiplex panel -> slide/marker autocorrelation -> patient means -> Max-T -> report, with durable resume.
Cells + markers/classes + optional annotations -> distance profiles, neighborhood composition and local marker maps.
Supplied polygons/classes -> bulk/front/bands -> architecture and optional cell/nucleus/bud/spot summaries.
Typed patient slides -> pooled counts/area -> composition/density/grid sensitivity -> patient-group tests.
Typed patient slides -> intensity-adjusted curves/nulls -> patient curves -> group comparison.
Typed cells + strata/radii -> best enriched circle -> repeat-the-search null test -> maps/tables.
Declared inputs -> compatible cached or new analysis -> stored result; the user selects and connects methods.

example_study_pipelines.question: Does MMR-loss staining form larger or more directional patches in one patient group?
pipeline: External cell detection and MMR label/probability measurement
MarkLab marked-section analysis
Declare patient-level scale/direction endpoints
Patient-group comparison
example_study_pipelines.deliverables: Per-section maps and curves plus patient-level effect estimates; no inference of molecular MMR status or clonality.

example_study_pipelines.question: Are immune cells concentrated outside the tumor, and does that differ between groups?
pipeline: External tumor/immune classification and tumor annotation
Boundary-distance profiles and cross-type/mixing measurements
Declare patient-level endpoints or use supported spatial-study curves
Patient-group inference
example_study_pipelines.deliverables: Immune density-versus-distance profiles, interaction summaries and group contrasts.

example_study_pipelines.question: Do fragmentation, budding candidates and nuclear alignment change near the invasive front?
pipeline: External epithelium/architecture annotations and nuclear measurements
MarkLab pathology architecture
Inspect front/band and budding outputs
Aggregate declared patient endpoints for any group comparison
example_study_pipelines.deliverables: Front-distance architecture tables, nuclear summaries, reviewed budding candidates and spatial overlays.

example_study_pipelines.question: Which multiplex markers have different spatial organization across patient groups?
pipeline: External segmentation and multiplex quantification
Map calibrated cells/channels/patients into a study recipe
MarkLab study run
Review marker-level patient tests and missing-data diagnostics
example_study_pipelines.deliverables: Slide marker-autocorrelation summaries and multiplicity-adjusted patient-group results.

example_study_pipelines.question: Does morphology add information beyond a measured marker panel?
pipeline: External image embeddings and marker measurement
Identity-aligned cell/patch summaries or registered modalities
Patient-level feature and held-out split declaration
Complementarity/fusion evaluation
example_study_pipelines.deliverables: Held-out feature comparisons and prediction diagnostics; a research evaluation rather than an automatic biomarker claim.

example_study_pipelines.question: How does a spatial transcriptomic spot's expression relate to nearby architecture?
pipeline: External expression processing and spot-to-slide registration
MarkLab architecture coverage/front-distance calculation
Join spot summaries to expression by spot ID
Explicit downstream expression-association model
example_study_pipelines.deliverables: Spot-level histologic coverage fractions and front context; expression modeling is a separate step.

output_products.local: Cell/spot annotations, neighborhood composition, distances, local statistics and selected hotspot/territory layers.
output_products.region_or_slide: Counts, densities, architecture summaries, spatial curves, structural features and QC/availability diagnostics.
output_products.patient_or_study: Patient endpoint tables/curves, effects, uncertainty, adjusted tests and selected model/prediction results.
output_products.files: Workflow-dependent JSON, CSV/Parquet, GeoJSON, SVG and Markdown reports; use recorded transforms for image overlays.

research_limits: Methods must match the inputs and sampling design; this is not a turnkey raw-slide-to-diagnosis system.
Measured and predicted labels remain distinct, and segmentation/registration choices can affect results.

Implementation and scientific validation are separate. Many advanced methods remain Research; some documented estimators and patient workflows have scoped public-data agreement. No workflow currently meets every documented Core criterion.
Within-slide spatial association does not establish population effects, clonality, signaling, causation or clinical utility.
